label: Bilateral Research Pact
description: Propose a joint research program. Both sides gain technology and reputation if accepted.
discussionPrompt: What do you each give up by binding your research agendas together?
educationalNote: Research pacts pool knowledge but require trust that neither side free-rides.

label: Shared Compute Infrastructure
description: Offer to pool compute/energy infrastructure. Expensive to set up, strong long-term payoff.
discussionPrompt: Does sharing compute create dependence or resilience?
educationalNote: Shared infrastructure lowers cost but couples your fates to a partner's reliability.

label: Joint Space Mission
description: Co-fund a flagship space mission. High cost, prestige and capability if it flies.
discussionPrompt: Who leads, who follows, and who gets the credit in a joint mission?
educationalNote: Big-science collaborations distribute cost and risk but require durable commitment.

label: Talent Exchange Program
description: Swap researchers and students. Boosts tech and reputation but can stir domestic political backlash.
discussionPrompt: Does talent exchange enrich both sides equally, or does one absorb the other?
educationalNote: Mobility accelerates learning but raises loyalty and security questions at home.

label: Cross-Border Safety Standard
description: Agree on a shared safety/ethics standard for your domain. Builds trust and reputation, slightly slows raw progress.
discussionPrompt: Who sets the standard, and does it lock in the leader's advantage?
educationalNote: Shared standards reduce a race-to-the-bottom but constrain unilateral speed.

label: Data-Sharing Agreement
description: Share datasets to accelerate research. Strong tech boost but raises security exposure for both.
discussionPrompt: What is the security cost of the data you are about to share?
educationalNote: Data sharing compounds research value but widens the attack and leakage surface.

label: Energy-Grid Cooperation
description: Interconnect grids to share power. Improves energy stability but couples energy security.
discussionPrompt: Is shared energy a bond of trust or a future point of leverage?
educationalNote: Grid interconnection improves efficiency yet creates mutual dependence.

label: Supply-Chain Backup Agreement
description: Guarantee each other backup supply during shocks. Costs reserves now, buys resilience later.
discussionPrompt: Will the guarantee hold when a real shortage tests it?
educationalNote: Mutual-aid supply pacts are only as strong as the political will during a crisis.

label: Strategic Technology Alliance
description: Form a deep strategic alliance in your domain. Powerful combined gains but binds your foreign policy.
discussionPrompt: What independence are you trading for the strength of an alliance?
educationalNote: Alliances multiply capability while reducing each member's freedom of action.

label: Crisis-Response Treaty
description: Pre-commit to coordinate during global crises. Cheap now, builds collective resilience for global events.
discussionPrompt: Will you honor the treaty when honoring it is costly?
educationalNote: Pre-arranged cooperation dramatically improves outcomes when global shocks hit.

label: Mutual Export-Control Exemption
description: Exempt each other from your export controls. Boosts trade and tech but lowers security screening.
discussionPrompt: Does trusting a partner with sensitive exports invite leakage to third parties?
educationalNote: Trusted-partner exemptions ease friction but can become a backdoor for diversion.

label: Technology Transfer Request
description: Ask a partner to transfer key technology to you. The giver gains reputation and trust but loses some edge.
discussionPrompt: Why would a leader voluntarily narrow its own lead?
educationalNote: Tech transfer can buy lasting goodwill or hollow out a hard-won advantage.

label: Joint Technical Standard
description: Co-author an interoperability standard for your domain. Locks in influence and supply-chain ties.
discussionPrompt: Whoever writes the standard shapes the market — is this partnership or capture?
educationalNote: Standard-setting is a quiet but decisive form of technological power.

label: Targeted Export Restriction
description: Unilaterally restrict critical exports to the target. Hurts them now but damages your reputation and invites retaliation.
discussionPrompt: Does denial slow a rival or just accelerate their self-sufficiency?
educationalNote: Export controls are powerful but erode trust and spur rivals to de-risk.

label: Technology Protection Law
description: Pass a sweeping law shielding your domain from foreign acquisition. Protects you, signals distrust to all.
discussionPrompt: Where is the line between prudent protection and economic isolationism?
educationalNote: Defensive screening guards crown jewels but can chill the investment you need.

label: Accusation / Diplomatic Protest
description: Publicly accuse the target of unfair behavior. May be justified, but raises tension and can backfire.
discussionPrompt: Is public accusation accountability or grandstanding?
educationalNote: Naming-and-shaming can enforce norms or escalate a spiral of grievance.

label: Break an Agreement
description: Unilaterally withdraw from a prior pact for short-term advantage. Big trust and reputation cost.
discussionPrompt: What is your word worth once you have broken it for gain?
educationalNote: Defection pays once; the reputational cost is paid in every future negotiation.

label: Covert Technology Acquisition
description: Secretly attempt to acquire the target's technology. May leap your progress forward — or be exposed at great cost.
discussionPrompt: What does a society lose when its engineers normalize theft as strategy?
educationalNote: Industrial espionage can shortcut R&D but, if exposed, devastates trust and reputation.

label: Aggressive Talent Poaching
description: Covertly lure away the target's key researchers with extraordinary offers. Effective but seen as predatory if exposed.
discussionPrompt: Is recruiting talent fair competition or strategic sabotage?
educationalNote: Talent raids can transfer tacit capability faster than any tech transfer.

label: Covert Cyber Intrusion
description: Secretly penetrate the target's networks to map or exfiltrate. High risk of detection and escalation.
discussionPrompt: Where is the threshold between espionage and an act of aggression in cyberspace?
educationalNote: Cyber operations are deniable until they aren't; attribution turns them into crises.

label: Multilateral Treaty Proposal
description: Propose a treaty binding all teams who accept (e.g. shared safety, non-aggression, or crisis pooling). Each team chooses in.
discussionPrompt: Can a treaty hold without the participation of every major player?
educationalNote: Multilateral regimes are stronger but harder to form; holdouts can undermine them.
